entities.summary: Paul-Thérèse-David d'Astros was a French Roman Catholic Cardinal and archbishop, born on October 15, 1772, in Tourves, France, and died on September 29, 1851, in Paris. He was appointed as Archbishop of Reims in 1817, a position he held until his death. D'Astros played a significant role in the Napoleonic Wars, serving as a diplomatic envoy for the Catholic Church. He was a key figure in the restoration of the Bourbon monarchy in France after Napoleon's defeat. In 1821, he was elected Cardinal-Priest of the Roman Catholic Church, a position he held until his death. He was a prominent figure in the French Catholic Church during the 19th century, advocating for the rights of the clergy and the poor. D'Astros was also a patron of the arts, supporting several artists and writers during his lifetime. He was a prolific writer, publishing several books on theology and history. His legacy continues to be felt in the French Catholic Church, with many considering him a key figure in the institution's history.
